169:
In this chapter we will see to present two sayings from the Zohar which disagree with each other in their homily and which further disagree with the saying of the Gemara that was given above. The first saying is in Song of Songs from the Zohar (Zohar Chadash 84b) and this is what it says:
“And God created the two large luminaries etc.” [cf. Genesis 1:16, with “created” instead of “made”]. At first there were two lights [weighing each corresponding to the other as the companions have established, and we have established that these two luminaries were in one mystery], joined as one, and they were of one weight so that both were called ‘great’ as we have established. Not that the moon was at first large and superior, but that all the time the moon stands with the sun in one mystery, because of this, she [= the moon] is called in his [= the sun’s] presence ‘great ones’. The tail of a lion is a lion and is called ‘lion’.
The moon said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Is it possible for one king to minister with two crowns as one? But [it should be] this one by itself and that one by itself. He said to her: I see in you that your intent is to be the head of foxes1This refers to the end of Pirkei Avot 4:15: ‘…And be a tail unto lions, and not a head unto foxes’; go and reduce yourself, because although you will be head of them, you will have a reduction from what you were. And this is what the moon said: “Tell me, [you] whom my soul loves, where will you pasture?” [Song of Songs 1:7]. How then is it possible for you to lead the world with two crowns as one? “how do you cause to rest at noon?” because the moon does not have the competence to give light, and it is not possible for you to lead [the world] with two crowns as one, with the sun and with the moon, as for the moon, what light does it have at noon? Because of this, it is not possible for you to minister with two crowns as one. “For why should I be like one veiled?” How then shall I be wrapping myself at noon, when there is light and force of the sun? I will go and seize this, covering myself in shame before him [= the sun], and I won’t be able to minister before you, and you, how can you lead and minister with two crowns as one? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: Oh, I have understood you, go and diminish yourself, “if you do not know, o fairest among women” [Song of Songs 1:8], as you said before me that it is not possible for me to lead the world with two crowns as one, go and diminish yourself and you will be head of foxes, “go out in the tracks of the cattle”, go out and be the head of all these crowds and small armies below, and pasture them and lead them and be king of all lower ones and lead each one according to what is decided for it, and be ruler in the night. Certainly, go out and diminish yourself, and thus it is fit for you. End of citation.

[...] And in the Raya Mehemna (Zohar, Pinchas 247b) the Rashbi gave a third explanation differing from the two of them [given above], and this is what it says: “And on the heads of your New Moons” [Numbers 28:11]. Now how many heads does the moon have? But these two dots just as this: [image], the lower dot [is] the moon. Her two heads are two dots which are upon her: Segol [image of a Segol, the vocalization mark that can occur below a letter], [but] in the beginning it was a crown/Keter upon two kings just as this: [image of a Segolta] and it was a Segolta [the cantillation mark that can occur above a letter]. But after she [= the moon] said: ‘It is not possible for two kings to make use of one crown/Keter’, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: ‘Go and diminish yourself’, and she descended to the feet of the two kings just as this: [image of a Segol], and this corresponds to a Segol; what had been a Segolta was turned into a Segol.
And the mystery of the matter [is]: in view of the two dots of these two kings, it alludes in: “Bulls, sons of the herd, two” [Numbers 28:11], and in view of the dot [that is] the crown on their heads, it says: “and one ram” [Numbers 28:11], just as one crown/Keter.
After she said: ‘it is not possible for two kings to make use of one crown/Keter’ she diminished herself, also thus: “and one buck of goats for a sin-offering” [Numbers 28:15]. The ram of Isaac [referring to the Akedah in Genesis 22] turned into a buck, it was transformed from Compassion to Judgement, and it was diminished. And therefore “one buck of goats for a sin-offering”, and it did not say “for a burnt offering” [so that it would] be a crown/Keter.
And from where [is it known] to us that there is a descent with the sin-offering? This is what is written: “And he descended from performing a sin-offering” [Leviticus 9:22]. And why did it combine a burnt offering with the sin-offering in the descent? But [only] to teach [us] that in the beginning a burnt offering was the attribute of Compassion, but afterwards it was transformed to Judgement with the descent, and it was called sin-offering, yet everything is one [and the same]. And therefore ‘Let them bring upon Me an atonement’, upon Me was the moon [as a] crown/Keter for sure [previously] like this: וֹ, but afterwards she was diminished and descended to His feet, like this: וּ (in our formulations there is ‘just like this [image of a Segolta] ‘just like this’ [image of a Segolta]), and at that time: ‘Let them bring upon Me an atonement’, it was said about her: “She is the burnt offering…” [Leviticus 6:2], she rose up from His feet as it is said about her: “And the earth is a stool of My feet” [Isaiah 66:1] to say about her: “the heavens [are] My throne” [Isaiah 66:1]. And this is the mystery: “the Righteous One controls the awe of God” [II Samuel 23:3], who reverses Judgement into Compassion. And the mystery of the matter is “the stone that the builders rejected has become the head of the corner” [Psalms 118:22], just as HWHY YHWH. End of citation.
